net.lemnik.eodsql

Interface DataSetCache<T>

  • Type Parameters:
    T - the type being cached
    All Known Implementing Classes:
    ArrayDataSetCache, NullDataSetCache

    public interface DataSetCache<T>

    DataSet objects that are connected to their ResultSets may use a DataSetCache to maintain an in-memory cache of the rows that have been fetched. The primary purpose of a DataSetCache is to maintain idetifier equality for the fetched rows (ie: row1 == row1), therefore the default implementation is a weak cache (implemented with WeakReference).

    A DataSetCache is expected to be zero-based (like a List or DataSet).

    Author:
    Jason Morris
    See Also:
    Select.cache(), Call.cache(), DataSet

    • Method Detail

      • init

        void init(DataSet<T> dataSet)
        Initialize this DataSetCache, which will be used to cache rows for the DataSet specified here. There is generally no reason to store the parent DataSet, but it is given anyway.
        Parameters:
        dataSet - the DataSet that will be using this DataSetCache

      • isCached

        boolean isCached(int row)

        A quick check to see if the specified row is currently cached. This method does not guarentee that getObject will return a non-null value, but it suggests that it probably won't. If this method returns false however, it is assumed that getObject will return a null value, and that the object should be re-fetched from the database.

        The row passed into this method will never be negative, but any other value is possible. The cache is expected to be zero-based.

        Parameters:
        row - the row number to check
        Returns:
        true if the object is probably cached

      • getObject

        T getObject(int row)
        Returns the object at the specified row. If the row is not found in the cache, this method may return null. If the return-value from this method is null, the row will be fetched from the database.
        Parameters:
        row - the row to look for
        Returns:
        the value cached in the row
        See Also:
        isCached(int)

      • setObject

        void setObject(int row,
               T object)
        Sets the value of a row in this cache. This is generally called directly after a call to isCached(int) or getObject(int) to set the value of the specified row. The object value given here will never be null.
        Parameters:
        row - the row index
        object - the value of the row

      • destroy

        void destroy()
        Free's up any resources used by this DataSetCache. This method should also make a best effort to flag any used resources for garbage-colletion. No method in this DataSetCache will be used after this method is called.
